text:
The ink had faded to a bruised purple, barely visible beneath the yellowed parchment. My grandmother’s handwriting looped and crossed in ways that felt intimate yet distant, like a whisper from another room. She died long before I learned to read, so these letters were strangers to me until now. Each stroke carried the weight of forgotten meals and quiet kitchen rituals.

I traced the recipe for her famous apple tart with trembling fingers. The instructions were sparse, relying on intuition rather than precise measurements. "Bake until golden," she wrote, a vague command that demanded patience. It was not just a list of ingredients but a map of her presence. The house smelled faintly of cinnamon when I opened the drawer where it had been stored.

Her death certificate sat on the counter beside my laptop. I typed out the steps carefully, trying to preserve the ghost in digital form. The oven preheated with a low hum, filling the empty apartment with warmth. I placed the pie inside and waited. Time moved slowly.
